data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"As n grows the probability of reaching unanimous consensus tends to a constant strictly between 0 and 1; the only absorbing mixed states are stable matching cuts, and the expected number of such obstructions reachable from a uniform random start converges to a Poisson law with mean \u03bb \u2248 c for a small constant c, so the consensus probability tends to 1 - \u0398(1), i.e. a constant strictly between 0 and 1.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If every locally stable matching cut is reachable with uniformly positive probability from a positive fraction of starts, consensus probability \u2192 0","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If no stable matching cut is reachable from almost all starts, consensus probability \u2192 1","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the trapping probability p_n per edge decays like n^(-1/2), the Poisson limit fails and the answer could still be an intermediate constant via a different mechanism","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Cut size is a monotone Lyapunov function: a vertex flips to the local majority exactly when its cut contribution decreases, so every trajectory descends to a local minimum of the cut. Absorbing mixed states are exactly the 'stable matching cuts': each side induces a graph where every vertex has at least 2 of its 3 neighbors on its own side, and crossing edges form a matching, so every vertex on a crossing edge has 2 same-color neighbors (no crossing edge shares endpoints \u2014 a matching). In a random 3-regular graph (locally tree-like), the dynamics first burns the O(n) crossing edges down monotonically; traps are manufactured at the end of descent when the surviving cut is small. The last few crossing edges form a matching with constant probability; the per-edge trapping probability p_n at the terminal stage is roughly constant in n because the terminal cut is a finite object (constant-size neighborhood on the tree-like graph), so the expected number of terminal stable obstructions converges to a Poisson with constant mean \u03bb = \u0398(1). Hence consensus probability \u2192 1 - P(Poisson(\u03bb) \u2265 1) = e^(-\u03bb) + o(1), a constant strictly between 0 and 1.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
